specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** classical-orders-identifier
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify twelve described column features and buildings from our route as Doric, Ionic, or Corinthian, classifying at least 10 of 12 correctly on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** classical orders, base, shaft, flutes, capital, volute, acanthus, entablature, architrave, frieze, triglyph, metope, Doric order, Ionic order, Corinthian order (all defined in Part Three above). **Evidence of Mastery:** In the quiz, the learner assigns each of 12 cards to one of three orders. An assignment is correct when it matches the Correct order column in Content. Mastery is 10 of 12 correct on the first attempt. Opening the labeled anatomy drawings in the explore stage is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Any column with scrolls on the capital must be Corinthian (cards 2 and 11). (2) Fluting tells the order on its own; in fact Ionic and Corinthian share the same 24-flute pattern (card 6). (3) All Greek temples are Doric (card 9). (4) Smooth, unfluted shafts belong to one particular order; they occur in all three (card 12). **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying is an Understand task: the learner must map a feature to the concept it signals. An explore stage with three labeled side-by-side columns builds the vocabulary; the quiz then mixes isolated features with whole buildings, so the learner must transfer the rule from parts to real monuments on the route. **Content:** Explore stage: three columns drawn side by side, each with these labeled parts that reveal a one-sentence definition when selected. - Doric: no base; shaft with about 20 sharp-edged flutes; capital of a cushion (echinus) under a square slab (abacus); architrave; frieze of triglyphs and metopes; cornice. - Ionic: molded base; shaft with about 24 flutes separated by flat strips (fillets); capital with two spiral volutes; architrave in stepped bands; continuous frieze; cornice. - Corinthian: molded base; shaft with about 24 flutes separated by flat strips; capital shaped as a bell wrapped in two rows of acanthus leaves with small corner scrolls; architrave in stepped bands; continuous frieze; cornice. Quiz cards, in this fixed order: | # | Card shown to the learner | Correct order | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | A column standing directly on the floor, with no base | Doric | Only the Doric order has no base. | | 2 | A capital with two large spiral scrolls and no leaves | Ionic | Paired volutes without acanthus mark the Ionic capital. | | 3 | A capital shaped like a basket of acanthus leaves | Corinthian | The acanthus bell is the Corinthian signature. | | 4 | A frieze of grooved blocks alternating with square panels | Doric | Triglyphs and metopes belong to the Doric entablature. | | 5 | A fallen drum with about 20 grooves meeting in sharp ridges | Doric | Twenty sharp-edged flutes are Doric. | | 6 | A fallen drum with about 24 grooves separated by flat strips, no capital nearby | Ionic or Corinthian (either answer accepted) | Ionic and Corinthian share this flute pattern; the capital is needed to separate them. | | 7 | The Parthenon, Athens, 447–432 BCE | Doric | The Parthenon is the great Doric temple of mainland Greece. | | 8 | The Temple of Athena Nike, Athens | Ionic | Athens used the Ionic order for this small, graceful temple. | | 9 | The Temple of Artemis, Ephesus | Ionic | Ephesus is in Ionia, and its temple was one of the first giant Ionic temples. | | 10 | The Temple of Olympian Zeus, Athens, finished by Hadrian | Corinthian | Its surviving columns carry acanthus capitals; the Romans favored the Corinthian order. | | 11 | The Basilica Stoa in the State Agora of Ephesus, with bulls' heads on its capitals | Ionic | Its capitals have volutes, with bulls' heads added as a local touch. | | 12 | A smooth, unfluted column with an acanthus capital on a street in Roman Ephesus | Corinthian | The capital decides; unfluted shafts occur in every order. | **Provenance:** Features and proportions from the chapter sections "Classical Orders," "The Ionic Order," "The Doric Order," and "The Corinthian Order." Building identifications from the same sections and from Chapter 15 (Parthenon, Athena Nike) and Chapter 20 (Temple of Olympian Zeus). **Rules:** - Twelve cards, fixed order, one first attempt each for scoring. - Card 6 accepts either Ionic or Corinthian as correct; the learner chooses one of the three orders, and both Ionic and Corinthian score as correct. - Score is 0 to 12. Mastery is score >= 10. - The explore stage can be revisited at any time, but returning to it during the quiz does not change answers already given. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner opens the explore stage and selects parts of each of the three columns to read their definitions. 2. The learner starts the quiz. Each card appears with three choices: Doric, Ionic, Corinthian. 3. The learner chooses an order; feedback appears and the card joins a summary grouped by order. 4. After card 12, the learner sees the score and the summary. 5. The learner should notice that the capital decides most cards, that flute counts separate Doric from the other two, and that the buildings of Ionia are Ionic. **Feedback:** Correct: "Correct. [Why]" Incorrect: "This one is [correct order]. [Why]" For an incorrect answer of Corinthian on cards 2 or 11, add "Scrolls alone are Ionic; Corinthian needs the acanthus leaves." After card 12: "You classified [n] of 12. Mastery is 10." If n < 10, a "Try again" option restarts the quiz from card 1 in the same order. **Starting State:** The three labeled columns side by side, and the question "What does the top of a column tell you?" **Chapter Anchors:** Three Greek orders; Doric about 20 flutes and no base; Ionic and Corinthian about 24 flutes; Parthenon 447–432 BCE; the Basilica Stoa's Ionic capitals with bulls' heads; twelve cards; mastery 10 of 12.
